subtitle: Abstract words, and the little words that aim a sentence
words.intro: Germans have a word for the feeling that your duty is to do something you don’t want to. They also have Kant, who wrote 800 pages on it. A *philosophisches Café* lets you discuss him on a Tuesday, over cake, and then go home and not take out the bins.

grammar[0].fact: German makes philosophy out of ordinary words: *das Sein* is simply *to be* with a capital. That’s why it can feel so heavy and so plain at the same time. Heidegger made a career of it. You’re allowed to find this funny.

grammar[1].subheading: Focus words, where selbst stands, and erst or nur
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: erst or nur?
grammar[1].blocks[2].text: Time is *erst*: Es ist erst drei Uhr. An amount is *nur*: Ich habe nur zwei Seiten.
grammar[1].fact: A single little word in the right spot changes who’s to blame. *Ausgerechnet Max* is a complaint about Max. *Ausgerechnet heute* is a complaint about the day. Native speakers don’t think about it, and they notice at once if it’s wrong.

document.intro: A real bronze plaque with Kant’s most famous sentence, the one on the starry sky. It’s printed with hardly a space. Find *zwei Dinge*, then find what they are. It’s long, and it’s worth it: *der bestirnte Himmel über mir und das moralische Gesetz in mir*.
document.fact: This sentence is from the end of his *Kritik der praktischen Vernunft* of 1788. It’s also on his tomb. *Gemüt* is another word you won’t get into English: it’s mind and heart at once, and it’s where *gemütlich* comes from.

reading.intro: Tuesdays at Café Sokrates, 7 p.m.: *Kant und die Pflicht*. Dr. Brummer leads the group. Max has come for the cake. Frau Huber has come because the bins go out on Wednesday and it’s Jonas’s turn, and she has a question.
reading.photos[0].caption: Immanuel Kant: Er sieht aus, als hätte er keine Neigung.
reading.photos[1].caption: Kants Wohnhaus in Königsberg: kein Fenster zum Hof.
reading.fact: Kant really is said to have walked the same route in Königsberg at the same hour each day, so that neighbours could set their clocks by him. He never travelled far from his home town, which is now Kaliningrad, in Russia. Frau Huber would have approved of him.
